title: Five years after admission, income differs by admission category (2018 cohort)
question: What have earlier immigrant cohorts earned, and how do their histories differ?
dek: Historical taxfiler medians, 2023 tax year, in 2023 constant dollars. These are not forecasts for a new arrival.

findings.headline: Median employment income at year five: $70,300 for economic principal applicants and $26,400 for refugees
findings.detail: Canada; admitted 2018, observed 2023; taxfilers aged 15+ with employment income; 2023 constant dollars. Economic principal applicants: $70,300; Economic spouses and dependants: $41,100; Family sponsored: $35,800; Refugees: $26,400; All categories: $47,500. Composition, age and employment participation differ across groups.
findings.calc: Canada, Median employment income, admission year 2018, tax year 2023; no mixing of cohorts.

findings.headline: Employment income changes between years 1 and 8 for the 2015 cohort
findings.detail: Economic principal applicants: $41,900 to $65,500 (+56.3%); Economic spouses and dependants: $26,100 to $38,500 (+47.5%); Family sponsored: $22,800 to $36,900 (+61.8%); Refugees: $18,300 to $28,500 (+55.7%). 2023 constant dollars; changing taxfiler composition is part of this movement.
findings.calc: (median in 2023 / median in 2016 - 1) × 100, same 2015 admission cohort, each category separately.

findings.headline: Median wages at year five range from $35,600 to $59,200 across 24 comparable CMAs
findings.detail: Admitted 2018; tax year 2023; 2023 constant dollars. Highest: Hamilton $59,200; Kitchener–Waterloo $57,100; Victoria $56,900. Lowest: Sherbrooke $35,600; Windsor $38,700; Winnipeg $40,900. These are full CMAs of residence; provincial values and CMA parts are excluded from this ranking.
findings.calc: Median wages, salaries and commissions; admission year 2018; tax year 2023; total categories; full-CMA geography only.

charts.title: Median wages by CMA — 2018 cohort in 2023
charts.subtitle: 2023 constant dollars; same full-CMA geography and methodology

interpretation: Use historical cohorts as context. Their admission categories, occupations and demographic composition differ from those of today's arrivals.
Local medians are not a forecast of an individual's earnings.
methodology: StatCan table 43-10-0030-01; taxfilers aged 15+; price basis read from the publisher's footnotes: 2023 constant dollars.
Years since admission = tax year minus admission year. Admission year itself is not published; medians exclude zero and one-dollar values.
CMA ranking uses the same observation period and full-CMA geography. Provincial fallbacks and provincial parts remain visible on place pages but are not included here.
limitations: Taxfilers who leave Canada or stop filing are not represented; composition changes over time.
Income combines employment and self-employment in the historical chart; the place comparison uses wages, salaries and commissions.
No territorial observations; some smaller places only have provincial context.
